name: Abha International Airport
notes: GACA (General Authority of Civil Aviation) official 'Comprehensive Airport Service Quality Evaluation' report for 2023 (نتائج برنامج التقييم الشامل لجودة خدمات المطار), read as a Wayback capture (web.archive.org/web/20260121140338) of https://gaca.gov.sa/-/media/Files/PDF/Reports/2023-ATQS-Report-AHB.pdf?as=0&hash=90C19CF3F85116EE1E05DF090293DD5C. In the 'airport facilities and services quality' results table, category 12 'المصلى' (the musalla) is scored 53% in 2023 (49% in 2022), while category 16 'فندق المطار' (airport hotel) is marked N/A; a scored category implies the musalla exists and was assessed. The report does not give its location (terminal, before/after security), hours, wudu or women's space. Operator since 2022: Cluster2 Airports (تجمع مطارات الثاني); its site is a JavaScript app and its services page did not render via r.jina.ai. Not visually verified. A later 2024 GACA report for AHB is archived but is image-only (no extractable text). flydubai's Abha page lists only 'Cafeteria serving snacks' and shops (silence, not evidence).

spaces.name: Prayer hall (قاعة الصلاة)
spaces.location: Not stated (reported as prepared for Hajj departures, possibly in the Hajj terminal only)

notes: Secondary source only: El Bilad article 'مغادرة أول فوج من الحجاج من مطار وهران الدولي إلى البقاع المقدسة' (citing APS/وأج, about the 1447 AH / 2026 Hajj season departures) says the airport prepared facilities for pilgrims including 'تهيئة بهو المطار وقاعة الصلاة ومقهى ومطعم وغيرها'. The article does not name the terminal (international flights moved to the new T1 in Oct 2022; domestic, Hajj and Umrah flights to terminal 2 in Jan 2023 per algerie-eco), so the hall may be in the Hajj/domestic terminal only. Location, hours, wudu, women's space unknown. Official EGSA Oran site did not answer. Not visually verified.
